pageCache.pageTitle: Marlborough House Vinehall - Early Years Nativity
pageCache.text:
Early Years Nativity
What a magical week in Early Years! Our youngest pupils sparkled on stage during their much-anticipated Christmas production, A Twinkly Nativity. Families packed the hall for two heart-warming performances, each one showcasing the children’s confidence, enthusiasm and hard work.
For many of our Nursery and Kindergarten pupils, this was their very first Nativity - a huge milestone! They stepped onto the stage with excitement and bravery, filling the room with extra charm. Our Early Years team couldn’t be prouder of their dedication throughout rehearsals.
Reception pupils led the story with impressive speaking roles, narrating the Nativity with clarity, confidence and plenty of festive cheer.
The children’s enthusiastic singing filled the hall with festive joy - from upbeat numbers to gentle lullabies. And of course, the teachers’ comic rendition of “Please don’t knock at the Inn… for we are exhausted!” was a crowd favourite!
With sparkling costumes, heartfelt storytelling and plenty of Christmas magic, A Twinkly Nativity was the perfect way to begin the festive season.

pageCache.pageTitle: Marlborough House Vinehall - Marlborough House School and Vinehall merge
pageCache.text:
Marlborough House School and Vinehall merge
We are pleased to announce the exciting merger of two prestigious prep schools, Marlborough House School and Vinehall, effective from September 2025. The new school will be known as Marlborough House Vinehall and will operate on the existing Vinehall site, marking a significant development in independent education in the South East
This merger comes in response to the evolving landscape of the independent school sector, allowing both schools to thrive in the face of political and economic pressures. The shared educational philosophy and pastoral care ethos of Marlborough House School and Vinehall will continue to flourish, emphasising the development of each child’s unique talents.
The legal merger will take effect during this academic year, with the full practical merger and move to the Vinehall site being completed by September 2025.
News Updates
A Shared Vision for Excellence in Education
For well over 100 years, these two prestigious and high-achieving schools have built an outstanding reputation for educational provision based on high standards of teaching, small class sizes, exceptional levels of individual support and first class facilities, within idyllic and stimulating environments. Both schools' most recent ISI Inspection reports confirm this.
As registered charities, the merger strengthens the core mission of both schools: to provide an outstanding educational experience focused on the holistic development of each pupil. As part of the Repton Family of Schools, Marlborough House Vinehall will benefit from enhanced resources, financial stability, and access to a global network of educational opportunities. The collaboration promises a bright future for the School, with continued investment in academic programmes, the arts and sport, a range of extra-curricular activities, and pastoral care.
Daniel Lewis, Chair of Governors at Vinehall, and Simon Hodson, Chair of Governors at Marlborough House, have both expressed their enthusiasm for the merger, stating: "This merger represents an exciting step forward for both schools. Working together, we will ensure outstanding provision, bolster admissions, and safeguard the future and traditions of our schools in these changing times."
Outstanding Opportunities
Marlborough House Vinehall will offer an exceptional child-centred, individualised approach to education from ages 2 to 13. The School will provide a vibrant educational environment for both day and boarding pupils, with a curriculum designed to balance academic rigour with artistic, sporting and personal development. Staff and pupils will benefit from collaboration with the wider Repton Family of Schools, gaining access to expert teaching, innovative resources, and new opportunities for professional growth.
Boarding will be at the heart of a Marlborough House Vinehall education, thus continuing both schools’ tradition of fostering a strong sense of community, lifelong friendships, and personal confidence. Full, weekly and flexi-boarding will be available.
The merger ensures that Marlborough House Vinehall’s pupils will receive the best preparation for their senior school of choice, and will enable development towards offering the very finest in 21st century education.
Leadership and Governance
Marlborough House Vinehall will be led by Mr Eddy Newton, current Head of Marlborough House School and a former Chair of IAPS (Independent Association of Prep Schools). A newly formed Board of Governors, comprising members from both schools, will oversee the governance of the merged institution, ensuring a seamless transition and a continued focus on educational excellence.
Eddy Newton, Headmaster of Marlborough House, remarked: "Establishing Marlborough House Vinehall allows us to combine the best of both schools as we strive to maintain excellent provision, value for money and the finest all-round education. Together, we will continue to provide an inspiring and nurturing environment that prepares our pupils for the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead."
About Repton Family of Schools
The Repton Family of Schools is a globally recognised group of schools that values individual growth, community, and academic excellence. With schools in the UK and internationally, RFS is dedicated to preparing pupils for the world beyond school, fostering a culture of lifelong learning and leadership.
“This merger ensures a bright future for these two wonderful Prep schools. We are delighted to welcome Marlborough House pupils into the Repton family and believe the new Marlborough House Vinehall School represents a genuinely exciting development in education in the South East.” Mark Semmence, Headmaster of Repton School and CEO of the Repton Family of Schools

Personalised Learning
At the heart of our school is a strong commitment to the individual care, development and welfare of every pupil. Our Personalised Learning provision is designed to help all children become confident, independent learners, able to reach their full potential.
We place great emphasis on early identification of learning needs, enabling timely and appropriate intervention to support progress and well-being from the earliest stages. When a child needs additional support, we work closely with staff and parents to understand their needs and agree the most appropriate steps forward. This may include differentiated classroom strategies, small group work, or one-to-one specialist teaching.
Our experienced Personalised Learning team works across the age range and supports a variety of needs, including dyslexia, dyspraxia, autism, ADHD, social and emotional challenges, and low self-esteem. We aim to provide an education that is tailored to each child’s individual profile, helping them overcome barriers to learning in a calm, positive and engaging environment.
We use in-house assessments to inform our teaching, and each pupil’s progress is regularly reviewed in partnership with parents and staff, ensuring support remains appropriate and effective throughout their school journey.
Where needed, we liaise with external professionals such as Educational Psychologists, Speech and Language Therapists and Occupational Therapists, and can support families in arranging formal assessments. We also ensure that, as children prepare for senior school entry, they receive the guidance they need to approach assessments with confidence, including advice on ISEB access arrangements where appropriate.
We believe in encouraging self-awareness and pupil voice, helping children understand their own learning styles, celebrate their strengths, and develop the confidence to advocate for their needs. Wherever possible, support is integrated into the classroom so pupils can learn alongside their peers and share in the full educational experience.
Our well-resourced and welcoming department includes dedicated teaching spaces and a sensory/therapy room, offering a safe environment where children can focus on areas of difficulty without feeling exposed or under pressure. Support sessions are designed to be engaging and fun, building resilience, independence and a love of learning.
All staff receive training in inclusive teaching approaches, and thePersonalised Learning team plays an active role in sharing expertise across the school, as well as with other schools and local organisations. Together, we foster a whole-school culture of inclusion and understanding, where every child can thrive.

pageCache.text:
MHV Holiday club
It has been a truly spooktacular week at MHV Holiday Club, as children embraced the magic and excitement of Halloween through a wide range of creative activities, outdoor adventures and festive fun.
From the moment the week began, the holiday club was filled with laughter, imagination and Halloween spirit. Pupils enthusiastically took part in creepy crafts, designing and creating their own spooky masterpieces using a variety of materials. From ghosts and bats to witches and pumpkins, the children showed wonderful creativity and pride in their work.
One of the highlights of the week was the ever-popular pumpkin carving sessions. With great care and concentration, children transformed ordinary pumpkins into glowing works of art, each with its own unique personality. The finished creations were proudly displayed, bringing a warm autumn glow to the holiday club.
The excitement continued with a lively Halloween disco, where children enjoyed dancing with friends, playing games and celebrating together in their fantastic fancy dress costumes. From classic witches and skeletons to imaginative and original characters, the costumes added colour, fun and a sense of celebration to the occasion.
Beyond the Halloween-themed activities, pupils also made the most of MHV’s beautiful grounds. Autumn provided the perfect backdrop for outdoor exploration, with children enjoying seasonal walks and discovering the many changes taking place in nature. From spotting colourful falling leaves to observing autumn wildlife, these moments offered valuable opportunities for learning and appreciation of the natural world.
Halloween has become one of the most anticipated times of year at MHV Holiday Club, bringing together creativity, friendship and outdoor adventure. The week not only provided memorable experiences and festive fun, but also encouraged children to explore, imagine and enjoy the unique atmosphere of the autumn season.
It was a joyful and engaging week for all involved, and a wonderful example of the vibrant experiences that make MHV Holiday Club such a special place.

Nursery & Kindergarten
Why Choose Us?
At the heart of our pedagogy is the wisdom of Maria Montessori: "The greatest gifts we can give children are the roots of responsibility and the wings of independence." Little Vines Nursery and Kindergarten nurtures these gifts through a learning environment that values independence, connection and real-life opportunities. Our holistic approach is centred on individualised instruction from our caring and highly qualified staff and on self-paced learning, acknowledging that every child is unique and develops at their own pace.
In Little Vines' calm and beautiful surroundings children are given the time and space to develop a love of learning and become fully themselves as well as making outstanding progress.
Parents and carers make a crucial difference to children's outcomes. We work closely with our families to offer continual guidance and support to ensure the best outcomes for their child at every stage of their educational journey. Parents must feel included, listened to and trusted within their own role, supporting their child’s wellbeing, development and learning. We offer parental workshops each term on a range of subjects; recent examples include Good Routines, Nurturing Safe and Healthy Eating Habits and Wellbeing. Our door is always open for a chat!
Sarah Wolford, Head of Nursery & Kindergarten
Nursery & Kindergarten Life
We offer wrap-around care for all pupils for 50 weeks of the year and a range of after-school clubs, giving parents the option of flexible times to fit in with work and family commitments.
For Nursery and Kindergarten children, this runs from 8.00am to 5.30pm all year round.
We recommend that children attend a minimum of three morning sessions per week in Nursery and four morning sessions per week in Kindergarten. This is to provide the best outcomes for all children, and to ensure that a routine is quickly and easily established.
We offer a bespoke transition package designed to suit the needs of each individual child. This often starts with a weekly invitation to our Messy Monkey toddler group on a Friday morning, which gives an opportunity to meet staff and other families, before more time is spent in the Nursery.

One of the things we absolutely love is how much time the children spend outdoors - it's such a refreshing change and something our son thrives on. There's a real sense of belonging here; not just for the children but for the parents too.
It’s amazing how my child has learnt all of these new skills and abilities, but is almost completely unaware that he is learning in any real way, as you and the team are so great at letting them find their way through just having a huge amount of fun. To be starting to read and write is amazing and it makes us so proud of him and grateful for such wonderful teachers.
I feel incredibly lucky to have found a school and nursery setting where the pastoral care and character building is focused on so amazingly and brought to the fore. My son has become so rounded and grown in confidence, and I’m sure that this is in no small part down to your guidance and input on a daily basis.

Open Days and Weekly Tours
Open Days and Weekly Tours
Visiting a school is all about the people: being able to meet the teachers who will be guiding and nurturing your child, getting a feel for the grounds and facilities, seeing our children and picturing your child amongst their new peer group.
Open Week: 12th - 16th October 2026
We warmly invite prospective families to join us for our Open Week this June at Marlborough House Vinehall School a leading day and boarding prep school for children aged 2–13 in the heart of East Sussex.
Come and experience the spirit of our school - meet our dedicated staff, see our pupils in action, and explore our beautiful campus and boarding facilities. Whether you are considering nursery, prep, or boarding, our team will be delighted to show you what makes life at MHV so special.
Book your personal visit today and see how your child can thrive with us.
Join us to see how we’re shaping the future of prep school education in the South East.
Private Tours
In addition to our termly Open Weeks, we run private weekly tours of our Nursery, Pre-Prep and Prep School 5 days a week during term time with our Head, Mr Joff Powis, and our Admissions Manager, Liz Powis.
Tours last approximately one hour; this will give you the opportunity to learn more about the Marlborough House Vinehall Nursery, Pre Prep and Prep School, see all our amazing facilities and meet our inspiring staff and children.
To arrange a private tour, please click on the link below or email us at admissions@mhvschool.co.uk or call us on 01580 883 090 and we will be in touch to arrange a suitable date and time for your visit.

Governors
Marlborough House Vinehall is a charity, run by a Board of Governors who are trustees. The school’s governing body has overall responsibility for the well-being of the school as a whole. They meet as a Main Board at least three times a year to determine the general policy of the school and review its overall management and control. In addition, there are two sub-committees: the Finance and General Purposes Committee and the Academic and Pastoral Committee; they also meet at least three times a year.
Simon hodson
Simon was appointed Chair of Governors of Marlborough House Vinehall School in September 2026.
He retired from being Senior Partner of international law firm DAC Beachcroft LLP in 2015 after a career that covered most aspects of corporate law. He now has several non-executive directorships covering a range of business activities.
Simon lives in London and is married with two children. He enjoys any sporting activity that encourages him to be outside
Simon can be contacted on: shodson@mhvschool.co.uk
Sarah greig
Sarah was appointed Vice Chair of Governors of Marlborough House Vinehall School in September 2026. Sarah is also the Chief Operating Officer for the Repton Group. Prior to that she was Bursar at Ashford School and Dover College, following her first career as an Army Officer, serving around the globe in various roles. Alongside her Army career Sarah competed in Nordic Skiing and Biathlon at National level, culminating in her appointment as a Team Manager at the 2018 Winter Olympics and a role at UK Sport running the Performance Investment Team, before entering the education sector. Sarah is married to Will, and they have two children at Repton. They have retained their base in the North Downs near Canterbury and continue to escape to the snow as often as life permits.
Ian mcintyre
Ian was appointed Vice Chair of Governors of Marlborough House Vinehall School in September 2026. Ian is currently Managing Director of the Repton Family of Schools and Ian brings a wealth of knowledge and experience in establishing and developing high-performing British schools around the world over the past 15 years. Following an early career spent teaching in UK independent schools including two Headships, Ian went on to lead the international development of Brighton College, opening their schools in the Middle East and South East Asia. Since 2019 he has been International Development Director at Rugby, responsible for developing Rugby's schools in Japan, Nigeria and Dubai.

Wu Liang, born in 1975 in China, graduated from the School of Water Resources and Hydropower Engineering of Wuhan University with a Bachelors degree in Building Engineering. Mr. Wu was appointed as Senior Engineer and Senior Project Manager on various large-scale infrastructure projects and worked in the one of the largest construction companies in China. He founded his own construction and landscaping company in 2000 and has successfully led the company for over 20 years, serving first as the company Supervisor and then as General Manager until 2021 when he sold his controlling share in the company and emigrated to the UK.

Pastoral Care
Supporting every pupil to write his or her own story starts with the quality of pastoral care at Marlborough House Vinehall. Embedded in our pastoral care, or our People Care, are our values of Empathy, Respect, Courage and Ambition.
Pastoral care is all-encompassing, forming not only the day-to-day support for pupils, but, in essence, the wider culture of the school. Ours is a school where every individual, pupil or staff member, is supported to reach their full potential.
The family feel of our school, enhanced by its size and deliberately high adult : pupil ratio, helps create the right environment where every person is known. Here, nobody is just a face or a number; they are an individual with a story to tell, each valued for their uniqueness and contribution to our school family.
Marlborough House Vinehall is proud of its deliberate care for the individual, the capturing of childhood and instilling of a grounded education that prepares children for the future, whilst holding on to the best things of childhood: playing in the mud, climbing trees, exploring far and wide. To bring this about requires a very dedicated and deliberate team of teachers.
Form Tutors are the backbone of our pastoral care network. The key point of contact between home and school, Form Tutors are our pupils’ greatest allies. Form Tutors take great pride in their individual forms and champion each child. Special threads of competitiveness encourage our pupils to do just a little more, work a little harder, push a little further.
With a strong pastoral culture setting high expectations, our pupils develop good manners, kind hearts, and enough grit to be able to face challenges and get back up when things are tricky. With this combination, we are confident that the future is bright for our young people.

Clubs
At MHV, we believe that a well-rounded education extends far beyond the traditional classroom. Our rich and varied extracurricular programme plays a vital role in nurturing the whole child - building confidence, curiosity, and key life skills that are essential in today’s fast-evolving world.
Our extracurricular programme offers an exciting and diverse range of clubs and activities, carefully curated to cater to a wide spectrum of interests and talents. Whether it's creative arts, music, sports, science, coding, or drama, there is something to inspire every child. These clubs are delivered by passionate members of staff as well as expert external providers, ensuring high-quality experiences across the board.
Each term, pupils are given the opportunity to choose from an extensive and evolving list of activities. Many clubs become firm favourites, with children returning term after term, building skills and friendships along the way.
In addition to the after-school and lunchtime offerings, pupils in the Prep School enjoy a unique opportunity to further enrich their school experience during the academic day. Every Friday, children take part in a timetabled activity of their choice - ranging from outdoor adventures to team challenges - fostering creativity, collaboration, and a love of learning in a more informal setting.
At MHV, extracurricular life is not just an add-on; it’s a vibrant and integral part of our educational ethos - where exploration, enthusiasm, and personal growth are celebrated at every step.
